topic: rooppur nuclear plant begins power generation testing
headline_marked: Bangladesh enters nuclear power era as Rooppur plant begins [[testing power generation]]
headline: Bangladesh enters nuclear power era as Rooppur plant begins testing power generation
summary: Unit 1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has started the process of generating electricity, a significant milestone for Bangladesh's energy sector. The plant is expected to supply 2,400 megawatts to the national grid once fully operational.
details: Unit 1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant commenced its electricity generation process at 12:03 PM today, following regulatory approval to enter stage C. This marks a pivotal moment as Bangladesh steps into the era of nuclear power.

The process began with controlled increases in pressure and temperature within the reactor, initiating a series of crucial operational tests. These tests are designed to verify the performance and coordination of various plant systems, including the reactor, turbine-generator, and safety mechanisms.

During stage C, reactor power will be progressively raised to produce steam, which will then drive the turbine to generate electricity. The plant's generation capacity will be incrementally increased while closely monitoring the turbine's functions.

While power generation testing has begun, electricity is not yet being supplied to the national grid. Unit 1 must successfully complete all tests under stage C before grid supply can commence, a goal officials hope to achieve by the end of this year.

The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, built on the banks of the Padma River in Ishwardi, Pabna, is a joint venture with Russia, costing $12.65 billion. It features two VVER-1200 reactors, with a combined designed capacity of 2,400 megawatts.

topic: jamaat announces 410km long march to kushtia
headline_marked: 1,500 vehicles to join [[11-party alliance's 410km long march]] to Kushtia
headline: 1,500 vehicles to join 11-party alliance's 410km long march to Kushtia
summary: The procession will travel from Dhaka to Kushtia, passing through Khulna, Jashore, and Jhenaidah to press for seven key demands.
details: The 11-party alliance is organizing a 410-kilometre long march from Dhaka to Kushtia tomorrow, Saturday. Around 1,500 vehicles and participants from 19 districts are expected to join the programme.
The procession will begin with an inaugural rally at the south gate of the National Mosque Baitul Mukarram at 7:00 am, with the march setting off at 8:00 am.
The route will pass through Khulna, Jashore, and Jhenaidah, concluding with a final rally at Shaheed Abrar Fahad Stadium in Kushtia at 8:30 pm.
The alliance is pressing for seven demands, including justice for the July uprising killings, control of rising prices, and an end to corruption, extortion, and land grabbing.
Other demands include the implementation of the referendum verdict, resolution of electricity, oil, gas, and fertiliser shortages, and an end to partisan influence in state institutions.
Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar stated that organisers will try to use one side of the highways to minimise public inconvenience.
The alliance has coordinated with police administrations in Dhaka and Khulna ranges, as well as deputy commissioners and superintendents of police for administrative cooperation.
Participants have been urged to maintain patience and discipline, with Porwar warning that provocative remarks or behaviour that could offend political opponents would not be tolerated.
caption:
A 410km long march with 1,500 vehicles is set to hit the roads from Dhaka to Kushtia tomorrow.

The 11-party alliance is organizing a 410-kilometre long march from Dhaka to Kushtia tomorrow, Saturday. Around 1,500 vehicles and participants from 19 districts are expected to join the programme.

The route will pass through Khulna, Jashore, and Jhenaidah, concluding with a final rally at Shaheed Abrar Fahad Stadium in Kushtia at 8:30 pm.

The alliance is pressing for seven demands, including justice for the July uprising killings, control of rising prices, and an end to corruption, extortion, and land grabbing.

Other demands include the implementation of the referendum verdict, resolution of electricity, oil, gas, and fertiliser shortages, and an end to partisan influence in state institutions.

Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar stated that organisers will try to use one side of the highways to minimise public inconvenience.

The alliance has coordinated with police administrations in Dhaka and Khulna ranges, as well as deputy commissioners and superintendents of police for administrative cooperation.

Participants have been urged to maintain patience and discipline, with Porwar warning that provocative remarks or behaviour that could offend political opponents would not be tolerated.
